# Part 1: Predict, then run

## Exercise 1

Write your prediction for each snippet in the text **before** running the cell. Then run it. If your prediction was wrong, explain why in one sentence; if it was right, write "correct."

```{python}
toy = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "a", "b", None, "b"],
                    "x": [1.0, np.nan, 3.0, 4.0, 5.0]})

left = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "v": ["p", "q", "r"]})
right = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2, 2, 3, 4], "w": [20, 21, 30, 40]})
```

**(a)** Prediction:

```{python}
toy.groupby("g").agg(total=("x", "sum"))
```

Explanation:

**(b)** Prediction:

```{python}
toy.groupby("g").agg(n_rows=("x", "size"), n_x=("x", "count"))
```

Explanation:

**(c)** Prediction:

```{python}
left.merge(right, on="id")
```

Explanation:

**(d)** Prediction:

```{python}
left.merge(right, on="id", how="left")
```
